hook: The address to which Stephen Tilton's house of 1872, built beside the Presidio & Ferries cable terminal, was moved.

parcel.year_built_note: As the 2025 secured roll and SF Planning both record it. Nothing consulted here reconciles that date with the 1872 house reported moved to this address; see historical_record and the page's unknowns.
parcel.property_class: 2 Dwellings on 1 Parcel, 4 units or less

historic_district.note: A spatial query against the historic-district boundaries returns no district for this parcel.

permits.description: a 304 sq ft pool with a 54 sq ft spa built in the back yard, with a certified safety cover and related equipment
garage enlarged — excavation and new concrete retaining walls, with no change to the street frontage or the garage door
renewal of the 2001 foundation permit for the remaining work
unreinforced masonry foundations replaced with concrete to give an eight-foot basement over the full footprint
a room added at the rear of the building

permits_note: Six of the 32 filings on this address are shown; the rest are street-space permits, $1 renewals made to obtain final inspection on earlier work, and interior kitchen, bathroom and deck permits.

historical_record.description: Stephen Tilton's house of 1872 stood near the centre of his lot at Union and Steiner Streets, beside the Presidio & Ferries cable train terminal, with a four-storey pump house and windmill on the property. It was later moved to 2460 Union Street.
